accept: patent ductus arteriosus with left heart volume overload

findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy with volume pattern

echoTasks.find: Continuous colour flow from descending aorta to pulmonary trunk at the ductal window
Dilated descending aorta with diastolic flow reversal on colour
Dilated left atrium and left ventricle with volume overload in the apical window

auscultation.murmur: Continuous machinery murmur grade 3 of 6 at the left infraclavicular area radiating to the back

exam.general: Preterm neonate day 5, on nasal CPAP, mild subcostal recession, pink in oxygen
exam.other: Liver edge palpable 1.5 cm, urine output adequate, umbilical lines in situ
exam.precordium: Hyperdynamic precordium with bounding pulses and a wide pulse pressure
exam.pulse: Bounding 150, palmar pulses full, femoral pulses present

history.a: Born at 30 weeks weighing 1.2 kg, now day 5, ventilated briefly at birth then CPAP
history.q: Gestation, birth weight and course so far

history.a: Increasing oxygen need since yesterday with more apnoeic pauses and a new murmur
history.q: What changed in the last day

history.a: Mother had preterm rupture of membranes, no chorioamnionitis documented

history.q: Any cranial ultrasound or eye screen yet

history.a: Expressed breast milk by tube with volumes built up daily as tolerated
No inotrope, caffeine started for apnoea of prematurity

keyPoints: Optimise ventilation and restrict fluids modestly while watching urine output and renal function
Start a cyclo oxygenase inhibitor course per the neonatal protocol where not contraindicated, with gut and renal monitoring
Repeat echo after the course to confirm closure and reassess left heart size
Refer to paediatric cardiology for ligation assessment if the duct stays significant or contraindications apply
Counsel the parents that the murmur reflects extra lung flow that usually closes with treatment or time
management.model: Supportive neonatal care with a protocol cyclo oxygenase inhibitor course, repeat imaging, and surgical referral if the duct persists

accept: continuous flow into the pulmonary trunk

stem: A day 5 preterm neonate born at 30 weeks in a district NICU develops rising oxygen need and a new continuous murmur at the left infraclavicular area. Pulses are bounding with a wide pulse pressure, and the precordium is hyperdynamic.
teaching: A continuous machinery murmur with bounding pulses in a preterm neonate means a patent ductus until proved otherwise
The ductal suprasternal window shows continuous flow into the pulmonary trunk, the defining sign
Left heart volume overload plus diastolic reversal in the descending aorta marks a significant shunt
Management is supportive care plus a protocol drug course, with surgery reserved for persistence
title: Patent ductus arteriosus in a preterm neonate
